e2a0fdb060: Is waist-to-hip ratio better than BMI?
47305e6f5d: They measure different things — BMI reflects overall weight relative to height, while WHR reflects fat distribution. Many health professionals consider them complementary rather than one replacing the other.
553d836497: Why do risk thresholds differ between men and women?
7d7e6ac784: Natural body fat distribution differs by sex on average, so WHO sets separate thresholds: a WHR of 0.90 or more for men and 0.85 or more for women indicates substantially increased risk.
07d79dfc33: What is a healthy waist-to-hip ratio?
7293721d3d: Using the WHO cut-offs, a ratio below 0.90 for men or below 0.85 for women is below the level linked to substantially increased risk of metabolic complications.
527c5279db: Should I use waist-to-hip or waist-to-height ratio?
90bcbfde71: Both describe fat around the middle. Waist-to-height ratio needs only one tape measurement and is recommended by NICE in the UK; waist-to-hip ratio is the measure used in the WHO report. Checking both, alongside BMI, gives a fuller picture.

823dad7c20: WHR = waist circumference ÷ hip circumference, both in the same unit. The World Health Organization's 2008 expert consultation uses these cut-offs for a substantially increased risk of metabolic complications:

8f4f965c51: Women: WHR of 0.85 or more · waist above 88 cm (35 in); increased risk from a waist above 80 cm (31.5 in)
77cd245b98: The WHO report notes that ideal cut-offs may differ between populations. The International Diabetes Federation, for example, uses a lower waist threshold of 90 cm for South Asian, Chinese and Japanese men.

a7395d9665: Where the body stores fat matters as much as how much fat is stored. Fat carried around the abdomen ("apple-shaped") is more strongly associated with cardiovascular and metabolic health risk than fat carried around the hips and thighs ("pear-shaped") — which is what makes WHR a useful complement to BMI. The thresholds differ by sex because typical fat distribution differs between men and women.
a2b5d085d8: The WHO protocol measures the waist midway between the lower edge of the lowest rib and the top of the hip bone (iliac crest), and the hips around the widest part of the buttocks. Stand relaxed with feet together, keep the tape snug but not tight, and read it at the end of a normal breath out. Measuring at the same landmarks and time of day each time makes changes more meaningful.

b670fa5c23: Adult guidelines commonly use about 1,200 kcal a day for women and 1,500 kcal a day for men as the lower end for a weight-loss diet without medical supervision. Very-low-calorie diets should only be followed under a healthcare provider's care.

bce195933e: Area scales with the square of length, and the circle’s size is set by one length, the radius. Archimedes showed that a circle has the same area as a right triangle whose legs are the radius and the circumference: ½ × r × 2πr = πr². In terms of the diameter it is π d² ÷ 4.
936b313aa1: How does the Shoelace formula work, and does vertex order matter?
fd3386234f: It sums the cross products of consecutive vertex coordinates around the boundary. Vertices must be listed in order around the edge (clockwise or anticlockwise); the absolute value handles either direction. If edges cross each other, the formula no longer gives the enclosed area.
7d7fcd0b72: How do I convert between square metres, square feet and acres?
97d1427e26: Convert the length factor and square it: 1 ft = 0.3048 m, so 1 ft² = 0.09290304 m², and 1 m² ≈ 10.7639 ft². An acre is 4,046.8564224 m² (43,560 international ft²), and a hectare is 10,000 m². The table above does all of these at once.

665bb910e9: Why do trapezoid and parallelogram perimeters need extra sides?
0afde42e03: Their areas depend only on the base(s) and the perpendicular height, but the slanted sides can have different lengths for the same height, so the perimeter cannot be found from those inputs alone.
